requirementFit.summary: The members-in-GET-/chats design removes the per-chat member requests (controller N+1 block and applyCompanionAvatar both deleted, pinned by a getChatUsers-notCalled mocha regression); the point-wise changeChatAvatar Store patch meets the operator requirement (no full refetch on one avatar change); the avatar ladder and meId handling are pinned by mapper tests.

implementationQuality.summary: Write-sets sufficient and verified against the code (api/index.ts is a pure re-export; utils/types.ts untouched; ai-assistant holds its own DTO copy; ChatAvatar already renders both URL forms; no migration needed). The default_factory analysis verified: POST /chats and GET /chats/{id} both return ChatResponse.model_validate(chat) and would 500 without the members default. Layers respect the guard: meId is a port parameter, the adapter never reads the Store.

evidenceQuality.summary: Round 1 rejected the unprovable 'exactly three SQL statements' claim; revision 2 pins what tests can prove: one IN query, zero per-chat member requests, uncapped /members regression pin (full list, user_id ASC), default-field regression, cap/order case. Gates match the repo evidence contract; the Windows-only ingestion-converter failures are documented as environment-specific and outside the write-set.

residualRisk.summary: Remaining risks bounded: unread_counts keeps its per-read-marker count shape (explicit out-of-scope debt), companion avatar freshness depends on the next list fetch (WS push is a non-goal), chatId-from-FormData is fragile under UI refactors but pinned by a test. One NIT-level wording ambiguity in Wave 1 item 3 ('same helper') is dominated by unambiguous statements in three other places and does not block freeze.

rounds.summary: Full review of revision 1: 1 MAJOR (the 'exactly three SQL statements' claim is false against ChatRepository.unread_counts — three statements plus per-chat read-marker counts — and unprovable by gates), 3 MINOR (cap could leak into /chats/{id}/members through the shared grouper; the three chats.test.ts avatar cases not all enumerated — 147-169 would stay vacuously green; the chatId source for the point-wise patch unspecified), 1 NIT (media test file unnamed).

Confirm pass over revision 2: all five findings closed across plan.md, acceptance-criteria.md and the manifest (not just plan.md); the SQL claim replaced by the provable one-IN-query/zero-per-chat-requests criterion; /members pinned uncapped with user_id ASC; all three avatar test cases enumerated (108-121, 123-145 -> N+1 regression, 147-169 deleted); chatId-from-FormData specified with the port contract unchanged; the launchGate documents the Windows-only converter failures. No new findings; freeze authorized.
